profile.campus: Silicon Valley (San Jose/Santa Clara), California (Equinix's founding market, Great Oaks/Corvin/Duane campuses)
profile.reading:
This building is Equinix's SV2 facility, part of Equinix's Silicon Valley data center network in the San Jose/Santa Clara area. Equinix was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson, both former Digital Equipment Corporation facilities managers, on the idea of building a neutral place where competing internet networks could physically connect and exchange traffic, a model that let the company grow through network effects as more networks joined; Equinix converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015 and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX. Silicon Valley, where Equinix is still headquartered today in nearby Redwood City, was the company's founding market, and its San Jose facilities on Great Oaks Boulevard and its Santa Clara facilities on Corvin Drive and Duane Avenue grew into one of the densest interconnection hubs in Equinix's global network as the company expanded internationally, entering Asia-Pacific in 2002, Europe via the IXEurope acquisition in 2007, Latin America in 2011, and the Middle East in 2013, and opening its 50th global data center in London by 2010 around the time it acquired Switch and Data Facilities Company. Equinix's own published specifications for the flagship SV1 building on this campus describe an 82,850-square-foot, single-story, steel-frame facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 2kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, and generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load; Equinix markets the Great Oaks campus for its direct connections to major networks and tier-1 cloud service providers. Equinix's website did not disclose this specific building's own square footage or power capacity separately from the SV1 figure cited as representative of the broader campus.

Pacific Gas and Electric, the regional utility serving most of Silicon Valley, and Silicon Valley Power, Santa Clara's municipal utility, have both cited sustained data center load growth across the San Jose-Santa Clara-Sunnyvale corridor in their own capacity planning, a dynamic distinct from the newer data center markets elsewhere in the country given how built-out and power-constrained the Bay Area grid already is after decades of continuous data center development since Equinix's own 1998 founding in the area.

reading.body:
Equinix SV2 is a 75,000-square-foot facility in Santa Clara, part of Equinix's founding market in Silicon Valley, where the company has operated since 1998 and maintains one of its densest interconnection hubs across multiple campuses in San Jose and Santa Clara. The facility offers N+1 redundancy for both power and cooling, with a minimum cabinet density of 5 kVA, but Equinix does not publish a total megawatt capacity for this building on its specification page. Without disclosed power capacity, this facility cannot be ranked against other AI-scale data centers, though its small published square footage relative to modern hyperscale campuses suggests it is designed primarily for colocation and network interconnection rather than consolidated compute loads.

Silicon Valley's grid is already power-constrained after decades of continuous data center development, a dynamic distinct from newer data center markets elsewhere in the country. Both Pacific Gas and Electric and Silicon Valley Power have cited sustained data center load growth across the San Jose-Santa Clara-Sunnyvale corridor in their capacity planning. California as a state has mapped 103 data center facilities but published power specifications for only 11, totaling 365 MW, meaning most facilities in the state publish no figures at all and are opaque to capacity assessment.

SV2 does not appear in California's published capacity tally because Equinix has not disclosed its power rating. This is typical: in a state with 103 mapped facilities, only one facility outside this one ranks higher in published megawatts, and most operate without public power specifications. Without its own published capacity, SV2 cannot be evaluated as a constraint or asset to AI scaling on the state grid.
